newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's L'Oreal reports higher 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: France's L'Oreal reports higher 1996 profits.

text.p: French cosmetics giant L'Oreal said Wednesday that profits rose 10 percent last year on sales growth helped by the acquisition of U.S.-based Maybelline.
L'Oreal issued an upbeat outlook for 1997.

It said operating profit jumped 17.6 percent to 7.3 billion French francs ($1.3 billion) in 1996, boosted by gains in both cosmetics and pharmaceutical activities through its 56 percent stake in drug company Synthelabo.
But a rise in finance charges due partly to the $760 million Maybelline acquisition trimmed profit growth on the bottom line.
L'Oreal reported its results provisionally in February.
L'Oreal's cosmetics business, which accounted for 81 percent of total sales of 60.3 billion francs ($10.4 billion), grew by 13 percent last year.
"Our cosmetics business grew nearly twice as fast as the global market and represents market share of 12 to 13 percent," said finance director Pascal Castres Saint Martin.
L'Oreal's brands range from the upscale Lancome and Biotherm lines to Redken hair products, the Vichy line sold in pharmacies and the Gemey and Jade mass-market brands.
With the acquisition of Maybelline, intended to spearhead expansion into emerging markets, L'Oreal further reduced its dependence on the slow-growing European market.
